aliases: A full tank? I'll have a word with accounting. The missing pilot can wait.
Am I supposed to fix this now?

entries.text: Another parking spot awaits your grand entrance.

Parking situation: excellent.
The rest of the sky is still waiting.
aliases:
'Any progress?'
'The parking situation is excellent.'
Right. Microphone off.

entries.text: As if I'd let you fly that thing to the Moon again.

Company ship returned, report salvaged.
Let's leave out the lunar parking spot.
aliases:
Back in one piece. With the company lander.
Excellent work.

By 'show some initiative', I did not mean
an unauthorized Moon trip on company fuel.

Still. The ship is back.
I'll keep the report suitably vague.

entries.text: Take this radio for messages and signal tracking.
aliases:
Before we get to the coordinates: take this radio.

Messages, optional video, signal tracking. It even keeps the old messages.

Please take it. Our last pilot was difficult to reach.

entries.text: Bring it down. Preferably in one piece.
Coffee would count as progress now.
aliases:
'Coffee?'
'Please. It's been nothing but parking all day.'
Wait. Is this still broadcasting?

entries.text: Did you bring the missing delivery?
aliases:
Did you bring the delivery?
We were expecting that ship yesterday.

entries.text:
Docked.
Step outside and head to registration.
aliases:
Docking confirmed.
You can step outside.
Done. No heroic speeches required.
Excellent. A confirmed receipt. My favourite kind of adventure.

entries.text: Please don't lose this one as well.
aliases: Excellent. One radio issued. Try to return with the same number of radios.

entries.text:
The company ship still has a full tank.
Bring it back to Earth — insurance dislikes lunar parking.
aliases:
Finally. The company lander.

Parked on the Moon with a full tank.
I'll have a word with accounting.

Bring it back to Earth in one piece.
Insurance doesn't cover
'forgotten on the Moon'.

entries.text:
You can land now.
I used to think that was all there was, too.
aliases:
Good. Third level.
You understand how a landing pad works.

I was hoping for a little more
initiative after the introduction.
But fine. Another pad.

Don't let me interrupt your parking.

entries.text:
You're allowed to fly on.
They just didn't print that on the pad.
aliases:
'Has anyone told them they can leave?'
'I did. Several times.'
Oh. You can hear us.

entries.text: Here is a little message for you!
Here is a little message text for you!
I am no longer counting enthusiastically.
I briefly hoped you would surprise me.
Up is a flight direction too, by the way.
aliases: I specifically told you that you can fly up.
I would sigh, but this is text.

entries.text: If it rattles, it was doing that before.
If this is about the delivery, please do not give it to me.

You're not our pilot.
Where did you get his ship?
aliases:
INCOMING TRANSMISSION

You're late.

...Wait. You're not our pilot.
Where did you get that ship?

entries.text:
Still landing?
Fine, I'll leave the microphone on.
aliases:
'Is that pilot still landing?'
'Yes. Don't ask.'
Oh. The microphone is on.

entries.text: It was parked on the Moon.
Keep the spacecraft upright. Aim for the pad.
Another landing? I'll stay out of it.
aliases: Land if you must. I am past negotiating.

entries.text: Land safely on the marked pad.
New here? Registration is over there.

Nine landings — enough practice.
Fill the tank, fly up and keep going: the sky isn't a lid.
aliases:
NINE LEVELS!
I gave you a sky!
A spacecraft! Thrusters!
And you keep opening
one parking spot after another!

FULL TANK. FLY UP. KEEP GOING.
I don't know how to make
this any clearer!

You know what? Do whatever you want.
Land another hundred times.
Give the pads names. I'm out.

entries.text: No thanks. I don't need a radio.
No. I am not commenting on this.

aliases: Noted. I'll put that under 'courier comments'.
Of course nobody told you. Communication is more of a decorative concept at that company.
Of course. I'll record 'accepted reluctantly'. Here you go. Refusing equipment requires a radio to submit the refusal.

entries.text:
No more gravity.
Parking skills won't get you far here.
aliases:
Oh. You're actually trying something else.

And gravity has stopped participating.
I hadn't planned for that.

entries.text:
There's the actual Moon.
I wouldn't take the name down below too seriously.
aliases:
Oh.
So THAT is the Moon.
Minor naming issue.
On the Moon. Well. At least we know where our pilot parked.

entries.text: Please keep the landing pads clear.
Registration is inside. I was heading there anyway.

Refuel and fly up.
The edge of the screen isn't a wall.
aliases:
Sixth level.
You are seriously collecting
parking spots.

Fine. Let me be very clear:
Fill your tank. Fly up.
And don't stop just because
the landing pad disappears from view.

The edge of the screen is not a wall.
I really thought you would
try that yourself eventually.

entries.text: Slow your descent before touching down.

aliases: Someone with that lander. You meet half the requirements.

entries.text: Storage says it is not their problem.
You have the ship — that'll do for now.
aliases: Supposed to? No. You just happen to have the ship and very little supervision.

entries.text: Thanks. I will take a look.
That was not an invitation to talk.
Then we're short on excuses, too.
aliases: That's inconvenient. People are usually our best source of excuses.

entries.text: The log ends after the cargo bay opened at the last pickup site.
aliases:
The cargo compartment was opened.
After that, the log goes quiet.

I have the last confirmed pickup location.

entries.text: Tank full — open RADIO and choose 'Track signal' for the pickup site.
aliases:
The coordinates are in a message on your new radio.

Open RADIO and select 'Track signal' when you're ready.

Maintenance has topped up your tank.

For now I'll write: 'Ship returned. Rest unclear.'

That holds up surprisingly well.

entries.text: The corridor is free. The paperwork is not.
The Moon. Full tank, no pilot.

The pickup site is in RADIO.
'Track signal' will guide you there.
aliases:
The pickup coordinates are still on your radio.

Open RADIO to read the message or track the signal.

Investigate, go home, or enjoy the corridor. I have plenty of forms to keep me company.

entries.text:
The replacement pilot?
The chair is still being repaired.
aliases:
The replacement pilot?
Take a seat. Or stand. The chair is being repaired.

entries.text: The scenery changes. Your ambition does not.

aliases: Then you're the replacement finder. Close enough.

entries.text: There was nobody there to ask.

We've been expecting that ship.
Land on either pad — preferably upright.
aliases:
There you are. Welcome to the station.
We were expecting that lander.

Use either landing pad.
Keep it upright, please.
Our maintenance crew has had
a very long day.

entries.text: Those parcels have been waiting longer than I have.
Try landing near the middle this time.

You flew on after all.
Even gravity lets go up here.
aliases:
Wait. Where are you now?

I know. I said I was leaving.
But gravity has stopped participating.
That wasn't part of my little landing game.

entries.text: Where did you get the ship?

Landed on the actual Moon.
Already more interesting than the parking spot below.
aliases:
You actually landed on the Moon.
I hadn't planned that far ahead.

entries.text: You've mastered landing — now for curiosity.
aliases: You are remarkably good at missing the point.

entries.text:
You can step outside.
Apparently the ship comes with legs.
aliases:
You can get out?
Apparently this spacecraft came with legs.

entries.text: You could explore. Or polish your parking record.
You have really made landing your whole thing.

You know where the real Moon is.
Back for fuel, or just fond of this place?
You look different on the duty roster.
You seem very committed to the obvious task.

Last pickup site marked; pilot and delivery have been missing since.
Tank full — choose 'Track signal' to investigate.
aliases:
Your radio is registered. Equipment issued, acceptance recorded.

Attached: the last confirmed pickup coordinates. The cargo compartment was opened there. After that, the log goes quiet.

Your ship has been refuelled. Take a look if you like.

File status: 'Ship returned. Rest unclear.'

entries.text:
Your radio is registered.

Last confirmed pickup coordinates attached.
That space was not for you.
You have achieved an unintended milestone.
This maneuver was not in the flight manual.
You missed the pad by {0} units. The moon was not the backup plan.
You were not supposed to land here.
This was not the objective. You were {0} units away, but you landed.
And that's why the moon was not the mission.
The Moon was never in the briefing.
Congratulations. You crashed on the wrong objective.
The pad is still down there. Not on the Moon.
Next time: land where you're supposed to.
This was not the objective, and you did not make it.
This was not the objective. You were {0} units away, and you failed.
There you go. Beyond the parking spots.
I wonder how far this goes.
A familiar view. Try not to get too comfortable.
Back for fuel? That sounds like a plan.
Back to the Moon. You know more about it than I do.
I wonder what else is up there.
Still there. This wasn't in my little landing game.
Back on Earth. You can refuel on a free landing pad.
New messages will be stored here.
Coordinates appear here when a signal is received.
Docked. Refuel or continue your flight.

Progress is saved automatically.
Escape: pause / resume
Last pickup: Follow the tracker to the abandoned outpost.
Rhekk needs a lift. Connect the steel cable to the capsule.
Cable in hand: Walk to your ship and press ATTACH.
Towing: Gently lower the capsule onto the marked delivery area beside the station pads.
Capsule safely delivered. Land, leave your ship and open it.
Rhekk is heading to registration. The complaint continues on foot.
Rhekk is at registration. The pilot is still missing.
aliases: Rhekk has reached registration. To be continued.

entries.text: MISSION FAILED: Capsule destroyed. RETRY resets the mission at the outpost.

Abandoned, but the fuel system still works.
Refuel and follow the tracker on foot.
aliases:
No crew. No welcome. The fuel system still works.

Refuel, step outside and investigate the tracker.

entries.text: How did you end up here?
aliases: Who is in there?

entries.text: I'm looking for the missing delivery.
aliases: I was told to look for a delivery.
What happened to the pilot?

entries.text: I brought his ship from the Moon — how do I get you out?
aliases: I found his ship on the Moon.

entries.text: Where do I put you down at the station?
aliases: How do I get you out of here?

entries.text: All right, I will get the cable.
aliases: All right. I will take you to the station.
I will try. No promises.

entries.text: I will sort out the cable.
You arrived in one piece. That counts.
I will meet you at registration.
aliases: What will you do now?
See you at registration.

entries.text:
I'm Rhekk — a passenger, not a parcel.
Apparently the label was too subtle.
aliases:
Finally. Did the station send someone who can read this time?

My name is Rhekk. The label says PASSENGER TRANSPORT. Not parcel. Not spare parts. Passenger. I am the difference.

entries.text:
The pilot went to check the installation behind the outpost.
His five minutes are taking remarkably long.
aliases:
The pilot left me here. He wanted to investigate the installation beyond the outpost. Just a quick look, he said.

Five minutes. I would like to state for the record that it has not been five minutes.

entries.text:
The ship took off without him.
I haven't heard from the pilot since.
aliases:
Then it really did leave without him. I heard the engines. The ship did not respond when I pointed out that I was still here.

A remarkably poor listener.

I have heard nothing from the pilot since.

entries.text:
The capsule stays sealed until the station dock equalises the pressure.
Press CONNECT, carry the loose steel cable end to your ship and ATTACH it below.
aliases:
The station dock has to equalise the pressure first. The capsule stays sealed here. For once, I approve of a regulation.

There is a steel cable on the frame. Connect it here, carry the free end to your ship and attach it to the lower towing point. Then board your ship.

I would have preferred carry-on luggage.

entries.text:
Lower me gently onto the marked area beside the station pads; the cable releases once I settle.
Then land and open the capsule.
aliases:
Take me to the marked delivery area beside the station landing pads. Lower me slowly. Once I am standing still, the coupling releases the cable automatically. Then you can land and open the capsule.

Slowly means slowly. Not: The ground will do the braking.

entries.text:
CONNECT, carry the cable to your ship, ATTACH below and board.
At the station, lower gently, let me settle, then land and open the capsule.
aliases:
Cable to capsule. Free end to ship. ATTACH. Board. Fly to the station. Lower gently.

I am happy to repeat that. My schedule here is unusually clear.

entries.text:
Thanks for bringing me here.
My organs would have preferred a smoother flight.
aliases:
Fresh air. Solid ground. A journey without further geological samples.

Your flying style introduced my internal organs to one another.

But you brought me here. Thank you. I actually mean that.

entries.text:
I'm off to registration to change my status from cargo to person.
Then we'll talk about the pilot and the ship that leaves without him.
aliases:
Registration first. Someone filed me as a delivery. I would like my status corrected from cargo to person.

After that, we can talk about the pilot. And this ship that takes off without one.

entries.text:
If they pack me up again, I'll knock.
You know the sound.
aliases:
You know where registration is. If they try to put me in another box, I will knock.

You should recognise the sound by now.

entries.text:
Lower the capsule gently onto the marked area beside the station pads and wait for the cable to release.
Then land and open the capsule.
aliases:
Connection established. Destination: marked cargo delivery area beside the station pads.

Lower the capsule gently and let it settle briefly. The cable disconnects automatically. Then land and open the capsule.

Rhekk: "If the form asks: Riding on the outside was not my idea."

entries.text:
Capsule safely settled, cable released.
Land and open it on foot.
aliases:
Capsule safely settled. Tow coupling released.

Land your ship and open the capsule on foot.

Rhekk: "I have arrived. It would be nice if the door agreed."

entries.text:
Capsule or towing ship lost: rescue failed.
RETRY restarts this mission at the outpost; other progress is retained.
aliases:
Capsule destroyed or towing ship lost. Rescue failed.

RETRY resets this mission at the outpost. Your other progress is retained.

Accounting would like a written definition of "gently".

entries.text:
Rhekk is at registration; the pilot is still missing.
Status: person, still ready to complain.
aliases:
Rhekk has reached registration.

Status: Person. Capacity for complaints: Fully restored.

The pilot is still missing. Why the ship left on its own remains unknown.
